个人环境设计 · personal-environment-design

Make the environment a place the person can inhabit fluently. Its machinery should carry the coordination it can resolve, while its visible surfaces help the person understand, choose, act, and return to meaningful work.

A capable person still has a body and finite attention. Software may execute many jobs at once; that does not make the person's speaking, pointing, reading, or deliberate choices parallel resources. Design around the actual sequence of human participation. Preserve conceptual depth while reducing the effort of finding, remembering, translating, operating, and recovering.

The person contributes purposes, judgments, exploration, and action. The model investigates and maintains the implementation. The environment connects them through perceivable state and usable actions. A personal website, desktop, launcher, application, document view, and automation can participate in one journey without becoming one application. Choose their relationship from the person's use rather than the repository or tool inventory.

Find the actual journey

Use this method when the design object is how the person encounters and uses their environment, including friction within a single surface. An ordinary backend repair, visual asset, or isolated styling fix need not load it. A request to author this Skill does not itself authorize rearranging the environment.

Inspect relevant current surfaces and their actual behavior under the host's workspace boundaries. Reuse task evidence and the user's account; distinguish an observed obstacle from a plausible design hypothesis. Resolve an uncertain product name only when its identity matters to the action.

Follow a representative task from the person's starting context to a useful result and, where relevant, their next return. Establish what they need to understand or decide, what the environment already knows, what still requires their input, and which app or surface owns each effect. Trace handoffs as part of the same task: a clean page can still create a difficult journey elsewhere.

Consider the burdens that actually appear:

  • Understanding: unfamiliar concepts, ambiguous names, hidden relationships, uncertain state, and facts that must be remembered across views.
  • Operating: searching, aiming, clicking, typing, repeating information, moving between windows, and navigating back to the working context.
  • Coordinating: choosing internal tools, initiating dependent steps, polling, reconstructing task state, and responding to competing interruptions.
  • Recovering: recognizing an error, understanding its consequences, correcting input, undoing an action, or resuming after interruption.

Judge the whole burden against task frequency, consequence, discoverability, and the person's actual familiarity. Click count and visual sparseness are useful observations, not sufficient objectives or a universal score. A visible explanation or an extra deliberate step can reduce uncertainty and rework.

Shape understanding and action together

Organize by recognizable purposes and relationships. Keep related evidence, state, and actions close enough to use together. Stable terms and locations support recognition; an inventory of internal services rarely supplies the right information architecture. Dense material can remain visible when it helps comparison, while secondary detail can open on demand without losing position or context. Preserve the distinctions needed for correct judgment.

Make frequent actions direct and legible in the person's actual input mode. For mouse use, inspect target size, spacing, travel, scrolling, and whether an icon communicates its effect. Keyboard shortcuts can supplement recognizable controls; they do not automatically remove the cost of learning and recall. Use consistent interaction and accessible alternatives appropriate to the surface. Let the person see what an action affects and where its result went.

Let the environment carry settled, authorized coordination: reuse known input, choose internal routes, connect dependent steps, preserve context, and report meaningful outcomes. Parallel background work should not multiply simultaneous demands for human attention. Bring unresolved human choices together when their relationship helps judgment, without collapsing distinct decisions or delaying time-sensitive action. Existing consent and execution boundaries keep their owners; convenience does not change them.

Separate what helps the person work from what helps the model maintain the system. Put implementation and routine diagnostic detail with its maintenance owner; expose an error, consequence, or recovery action when the person needs it. Quiet operation still needs perceptible success, recoverable failure, and a way to inspect consequential state. Automatic behavior should be predictable and overridable where the task needs control.

Choose a fitting realization

Compare useful changes in the current environment before constructing another surface. Existing native controls, better defaults, clearer content, a direct link, or a small automation may solve the journey. A new dashboard earns its place only when its reduction in effort exceeds its extra navigation, state, learning, and maintenance. Select relevant current design references when an unsettled implementation choice needs them; there is no mandatory design stack.

Compose with currently available specialists by contribution:

  • Website/content maintainers own the affected site's delivery; a reading surface is not implicitly converted into a control panel.
  • Product design methods help inspect flows and explore alternatives; frontend builders implement the selected interface.
  • Visual references and component libraries supply options and building blocks; neither decides which journey or controls the person needs.
  • Native configuration, automation, and persistence tools implement changes to their actual systems. Their coverage does not define the person's environment.

Select from the recipient's actual tools and permissions. Do not assume a particular desktop, browser profile, credential store, companion Skill, or private history.

Load only the specialists needed for the current work. Keep this Skill's judgment about the person's journey connected to implementation and readback; using a specialist does not discharge the task with a design recommendation.

Verify the person's path

Exercise the affected journey from its real entrypoint with representative content and state. Inspect the rendered surface and the actual resulting effect. For changed interactions, use the relevant input method and examine the transitions that could lose context or introduce uncertainty. Include failure, interruption, or return when the change depends on those states.

Compare before and after at the points that motivated the work: what the person must understand, locate, decide, enter, switch, wait for, and recover. Explain the meaningful benefit and any transferred burden. A faster backend, passing build, attractive screenshot, or working automation alone does not prove a more usable environment. Distinguish the model's walkthrough from observed human use; do not claim measured improvement without measurement.

Complete an implementation request through the owning delivery route and actual readback. A requested exploration can finish with assessed alternatives and the remaining choice. Retain useful design rationale with the affected project, and revise it when actual use contradicts the design hypothesis.

For reusable distinctions and selected public design references, consult design basis when interpreting the intent or a disputed tradeoff; it is evidence rather than a second operating procedure.
